title: Steam approved DeltaV, my strategy game built with AI-generated code and visuals. Here is a full match walkthrough.
author: va2k0r
selftext:
I've just received Steam's approval for DeltaV Orbital Strategy's Early Access build, and I'm preparing the launch. I shared a short clip here before; this time it's an 11-minute walkthrough of a match, from the opening decisions to the result.



I directed Codex to generate the game's original code and visual assets, including the simulation, interface and spacecraft. I set the rules, direct iterations and test the results. Music is separately licensed; third-party libraries, fonts and other source materials are credited separately.



One concrete constraint in my workflow: the simulation stays headless, and the renderer cannot own gameplay rules. That separation lets me change the visuals without changing what an order actually does. I use automated checks alongside playing matches to catch regressions in movement, fuel use and combat resolution.



In this match I try to win by cutting off the enemy's fuel. Every ship draws from the same fleet reserve, so moving one vessel can affect another's ability to survive an incoming missile. The walkthrough shows why I send a ship before its supporting missile, when I retreat, and how I deny fuel production.



If you watch a section, I'd be interested in where the consequences of an order stop being clear. Does the interface explain why fuel denial works, or does that only become understandable through the narration?



Steam page and free tutorial demo: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5070120/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5070120/)

Credits: [https://deltavorbitalstrategy.com/credits.html](https://deltavorbitalstrategy.com/credits.html)



Real player-versus-AI gameplay, with planning pauses shortened. The English narration uses a synthetic voice. Music: AlkaKrab, 30 Sci-fi Space Tracks. No generative AI runs during play.
